chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Suleiman, from Ismail ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Tameemi, from Husayn ibn Ulwan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no believer who supplicates for the believers and the believing women, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will return upon him the like of what he supplicated for them with, from every believer and believing woman who passed away from the beginning of time or who is coming until the Day of Judgment.'

Indeed, the servant is commanded to be dragged to the Fire on the Day of Judgment, so he is pulled, and the believers and the believing women say, 'O Lord! This is the one who was supplicating for us, so intercede for him on our behalf.' So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, accepts their intercession regarding him, so he attains salvation.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for supplicating for other believers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the cosmic scale of communal solidarity in Shia tradition, where a single supplicant benefits from the prayers of all believers across time. It illustrates the mechanism of collective intercession (shafa'ah), where the accumulated merit of the Ummah rescues the individual from Hellfire, emphasizing that spiritual success is inherently communal. This concept reinforces the Shia emphasis on the interconnectedness of the faithful, linking individual piety to the broader salvation of the community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Ismail Bin Ibrahim, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Tameemy, from Husayn Bin Ulwan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘There is none from a Momin supplicating for the Momineen and the Mominaat (believing women), except Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Return upon him the like of which he had supplicated for them with, from every Momin and Momina (beliving woman) of the past from the beginning of the time or the time coming up to the Day of Judgment.

The servant would be Commanded with to be dragged to the Fire on the Day of Judgment, so the Momineen and the Mominaat would be saying, ‘O Lordazwj! This is the one who was supplicating for us, so we are interceding with regards to him. So Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would (Accept) their intercession regarding him, so he would attain salvation’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Isma’Il ibn Ibrahim from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Tamimi from Husayn ibn ‘Ulwan from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Any believing person who prays for the believing people male and female, Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, returns to such person a reward equal to the reward for a likewise prayer with which all believing people, male and female have been praying from the beginning of time and all who will do so in future up to the Day of Judgment.

A servant will be ordered and dragged to the fire and the believing people male and female will say, ‘O Lord, this is the one who prayed for us, accept our intercession for him and Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, will accept their intercession about him and he will be saved.’”
